chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: The PBS show 'G.I. Jive' and television talk shows
summary: She sang 'Loch Lomond' with a full orchestra at Roseland for Public Television and made talk-show appearances.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay, the other notable thing you did very recently was the show you're talking about "G.I. Jive".
Yes. Oh yeah, you know that was the result of, I suppose, of having been in a production. This was a tie-in with the American Theatre
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Wing because they along with the Public Television Producers, they decided to do this show. The theme of it was, of course, had to do with the U.S.O. and Canteen, and so they decided to do this as sort of a nostalgia effort.
A reconstructure of World War II.

Yeah, it was taped at Roseland Stagedoor Ballroom and they had it set up with the, as the Canteen, with the coffee urns and the franks and the donuts and some ex-G.I.'s in uniform and they had this very large orchestra. And they had people like Hildergard, Maxine Andrews. They showed clips from some movie that the Andrew Sisters did. They had a clip there of Louie Jordan doing the G.I. Jive. And of course they had Cab Calloway, the Nicholas Brothers, Connie Haines, and several other people. Of course, I worked with a small combination. Just Derek Smith on Piano George Duvivieron bass and I forget who was on drums. And trumpet and tenor. And I did five tunes. I did "Troubles and Dreams" "I've Got The World On A String", "Harlem Butterfly", "A Hundred Years From Today" and "Loch Lomond" of course.
And the last one, I think you
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
mentioned to me before you did with the full orchestra.
Well they made a full arrangement of "Loch Lomand". They used part of "Loch Lomand" to bring me on, to introduce me. And then as my last number I sang "Loch Lomand" with the full orchestra.
Okay, and that's on the Public Broadcasting?

Yes, Public Broadcasting. It was supposed to have been shown several times since then. When I appear out in Long Island sometimes someone say, I just caught your show again, you know. So they got other outlets they distribute the tapes through.
